title: Formulas of binary compounds
competency: Write formulas of simple binary compounds using symbols and valences.

keywords.def: A compound made of only two different elements.
The combining power of an element. Most common elements have valence 1, 2 or 3.

en.text: A binary compound has two different elements. To write its formula: write the symbols, write each valence above, then criss-cross the valences to below the other symbol. Omit a subscript of 1. Calcium (2) and chlorine (1) give CaCl₂.

screens.title: How many partners?
screens.ask: Calcium has valence 2 and chlorine has valence 1. How many chlorines does one calcium need?
screens.after: Calcium can hold two chlorines. The formula is CaCl₂. The criss-cross method shows this.

screens.title: 3.2.4 Formulas of binary compounds
paras: Binary compounds are made of two different elements.
To write their formulas, follow three steps.
table: Write the symbols of the elements.
Write the valence number above each symbol.
Criss-cross the valences and write them below the symbols. Omit a 1.

screens.title: Example a: potassium iodide
steps: Step 1: write the symbols K and I.
Step 2: valences above: K is 1, I is 1.
A subscript of 1 is omitted. Potassium iodide is KI.

screens.title: Example b: calcium chloride
steps: Step 1: write the symbols Ca and Cl.
Step 2: valences above: Ca is 2, Cl is 1.
Step 3: criss-cross: Ca gets 1, Cl gets 2 → Ca₁Cl₂.
Omit the 1. Calcium chloride is CaCl₂.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A compound made of only two different elements.

screens.text: Use criss-cross to write the formula of sodium chloride (Na = 1, Cl = 1).
screens.why:
Symbols: Na and Cl.
Valences: Na 1, Cl 1.
Criss-cross: Na₁Cl₁.
Omit the 1s: NaCl.
Na₂Cl is wrong: neither valence is 2.

screens.title: Aluminum oxide
steps: Criss-cross: Al gets 2, O gets 3 → Al₂O₃.

screens.text: Use criss-cross to write the formula of aluminum oxide (Al = 3, O = 2).
screens.why:
Symbols: Al and O.
Valences: Al 3, O 2.
Criss-cross: Al takes O's 2, O takes Al's 3 → Al₂O₃.
Check: 2 × 3 = 6 and 3 × 2 = 6. Balanced.
Al₃O₂ is wrong: it keeps each valence under its own symbol.
screens.clue: Each valence moves below the OTHER symbol.

screens.text: Use criss-cross to write the formula of magnesium nitride (Mg = 2, N = 3).
screens.why:
Symbols: Mg and N.
Valences: Mg 2, N 3.
Criss-cross: Mg takes N's 3, N takes Mg's 2 → Mg₃N₂.
Check: 3 × 2 = 6 and 2 × 3 = 6. Balanced.
Answer: Mg₃N₂.

screens.title: Criss-cross steps in order
screens.text: Put the steps for writing a binary formula in order.
items: Write the symbols of the two elements
Write the valence above each symbol
Criss-cross: write each valence below the other symbol
Omit any 1 and simplify equal subscripts
screens.why:
Step i: write the symbols, for example Ca and Cl.
Step ii: write the valences above: Ca 2, Cl 1.
Step iii: criss-cross them below: Ca₁Cl₂.
Last: omit the 1 (and divide equal subscripts): CaCl₂.
screens.clue: You need the symbols before you can write anything above them.

screens.title: When the subscripts are equal
steps: Symbols: Cu and O. Copper(II) means Cu = 2. O = 2.
Both subscripts are 2. Divide both by 2.

screens.title: Simplify or keep?
screens.text: After criss-cross, does each formula need simplifying?
items: The subscripts 1 and 2 cannot be divided.
The subscripts 2 and 1 cannot be divided.
The subscripts 2 and 1 cannot be divided.
screens.why:
When both subscripts are the same, divide both by that number.
Ca₂S₂ → CaS, Zn₂O₂ → ZnO, Pb₂O₂ → PbO.
CaCl₂, Na₂O and K₂S have a hidden 1.
They are already in simplest form.
screens.clue: Look for formulas whose two subscripts are equal.

screens.text: Aluminum (valence 3) and nitrogen (valence 3) form aluminum nitride. Use criss-cross: what is its formula?
screens.why:
Symbols: Al and N. Valences: 3 and 3.
Criss-cross: Al₃N₃.
Both subscripts are 3, so divide both by 3.
Al₁N₁ → AlN.
Al₃N₃ is not simplified, so it is wrong.
screens.clue: Simplify when the subscripts can be divided.

items.text: Write the chemical formula for copper (II) oxide.
items.why:
Copper (II) means Cu has valence 2. O has valence 2.
Criss-cross: Cu₂O₂.
Both subscripts are 2: divide by 2.
Answer: CuO.

items.text: Write the chemical formula for magnesium nitride.
items.why:
Symbols: Mg and N.
Valences: Mg 2, N 3.
Criss-cross: Mg takes N's 3, N takes Mg's 2 → Mg₃N₂.
Check: 3 × 2 = 6 and 2 × 3 = 6. Balanced.
Answer: Mg₃N₂.

items.text: Write the chemical formula for sodium chloride.
items.why:
Symbols: Na and Cl.
Valences: Na 1, Cl 1.
Criss-cross: Na₁Cl₁.
Omit the 1s: NaCl.
Na₂Cl is wrong: neither valence is 2.

items.text: Write the chemical formula for aluminum oxide.
items.why:
Symbols: Al and O.
Valences: Al 3, O 2.
Criss-cross: Al takes O's 2, O takes Al's 3 → Al₂O₃.
Check: 2 × 3 = 6 and 3 × 2 = 6. Balanced.
Al₃O₂ is wrong: it keeps each valence under its own symbol.

items.text: Write the chemical formula for iron (III) oxide.
items.why:
(III) means iron has valence 3. O has valence 2.
Criss-cross: Fe takes 2, O takes 3 → Fe₂O₃.
Check: 2 × 3 = 6 = 3 × 2.
FeO would be iron (II) oxide.
Answer: Fe₂O₃.

items.text: Write the chemical formula for iron (II) bromide.
items.why:
(II) means iron has valence 2. Br has valence 1.
Criss-cross: Fe₁Br₂.
Omit the 1: FeBr₂.
Check: 1 × 2 = 2 = 2 × 1.

items.text: Write the chemical formula for silver oxide.
items.why:
Ag has valence 1. O has valence 2.
Criss-cross: Ag takes 2, O takes 1 → Ag₂O₁.
Omit the 1: Ag₂O.
Check: 2 × 1 = 2 = 1 × 2.

items.text: Write the chemical formula for calcium fluoride.
items.why:
Ca has valence 2. F has valence 1.
Criss-cross: Ca₁F₂.
Omit the 1: CaF₂.
Check: 1 × 2 = 2 = 2 × 1.

items.text: Which is the chemical formula of aluminum nitride?
items.why:
Symbols: Al and N. Valences: 3 and 3.
Criss-cross: Al₃N₃.
Both subscripts are 3, so divide both by 3.
Al₁N₁ → AlN.
Al₃N₃ is not simplified, so it is wrong.

items.text: What is the valence of aluminium? (The book asks how many valence numbers it has.)
items.why:
Table 3.4 gives aluminium one valence: 3.
Its ion is Al³⁺, with 3 charges.
Answer: 3.

test.text: Use criss-cross to write the formula of potassium iodide (K = 1, I = 1).
test.why:
Symbols: K and I. Valences: 1 and 1.
Criss-cross: K₁I₁.
Omit the 1s: KI.

test.text: Use criss-cross to write the formula of calcium chloride (Ca = 2, Cl = 1).
test.why:
Symbols: Ca and Cl. Valences: 2 and 1.
Criss-cross: Ca takes 1, Cl takes 2 → Ca₁Cl₂.
Omit the 1: CaCl₂.
Check: 1 × 2 = 2 = 2 × 1.

test.text: Use criss-cross to write the formula of sodium oxide (Na = 1, O = 2).
test.why:
Symbols: Na and O. Valences: 1 and 2.
Criss-cross: Na takes 2, O takes 1 → Na₂O₁.
Omit the 1: Na₂O.
Check: 2 × 1 = 2 = 1 × 2.

test.text: Use criss-cross to write the formula of magnesium oxide (Mg = 2, O = 2).
test.why:
Symbols: Mg and O. Valences: 2 and 2.
Criss-cross: Mg₂O₂.
Both subscripts are 2: divide by 2.
Answer: MgO.

test.text: Use criss-cross to write the formula of calcium nitride (Ca = 2, N = 3).
test.why:
Symbols: Ca and N. Valences: 2 and 3.
Criss-cross: Ca takes 3, N takes 2 → Ca₃N₂.
Check: 3 × 2 = 6 = 2 × 3.
Ca₂N₃ is wrong: the valences were not swapped.

notes.text: Formulas are chosen from options (typing subscripts on a phone is hard). Exercise 3.3 Q2 (naming) is in lesson 3.2.5.
Exercise 3.3 Q4 wording ("how many valence numbers") is unclear; asked as "what is its valence" (3).
